What I want next. I want to get off the bedside and into the side of healthcare where you figure out how the work should flow. I've been a nurse for twelve years and the parts I loved most were never the procedures. It was being charge and solving the puzzle, being the Epic super-user and translating between the nurses and the people building the system, and the virtual nursing pilot, where we had to invent the workflow from nothing.

So the jobs I'm looking at: clinical implementation, like an implementation specialist or clinical implementation consultant at an EHR company or a virtual care company, the person who helps a hospital or clinic actually go live and get their nurses using the thing. Or clinical operations, especially for virtual care or telehealth, running the nurse side of a virtual program, the workflows, the staffing, the metrics. Clinical informatics would be great too, I know that's harder to get into without Epic certification, but I'd take a nurse informaticist or clinical analyst role in a heartbeat if someone would sponsor the cert.

Companies that excite me are the ones doing virtual care or digital health that actually touches patients and clinicians, places like Quillfield, Bellwick, Medlattice, Dosewell, Fennel & Finch. I want a company that has nurses in the room when they decide things, not one that thinks nurses are just users.

What I don't want. I don't want to go back to full-time bedside. Part-time PRN on the side maybe, but not as my main job. I don't want sales. I've had device reps tell me I'd be great at it and I'm sure I'd make money, but I'm not carrying a quota and I'm not selling to my old coworkers. No clinical sales, no medical device sales, no "clinical account executive" that's really sales with a nursing title. And I'm not trying to become a software engineer. I took one SQL course. I like data and I'll use it, but I'm not going to be a developer and I don't want to pretend.

The hard stuff, plainly:

Pay. I need at least $95,000 base. Below that, honestly, I'm better off picking up more shifts as a nurse, so anything under $95k base is a no, I don't care how cool the company is.

Location. I live in Denver and I'm staying in Denver. Daniel's job is here and we bought a house. So it's hybrid in the Denver area or fully remote anywhere in the US. I won't relocate, and I'm not doing something that's onsite four days a week in another city either.

Travel. I can travel some, I know implementation means go-lives, but at most about 25%, so like a week a month on average. Not a road warrior job. I did that with travel nursing.

Work authorization. I'm a US citizen, so no sponsorship needed, and I don't have any kind of security clearance, I've never needed one.

Other than that I'm flexible. I'd take a step down in title if it gets me into the right company. I'd like to stay close enough to patients that I remember why it matters.
